etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English sprenkelen, sprynklen, from Middle Dutch sprenkelen, equivalent to sprink +‎ -le (frequentative suffix). Cognate with Dutch sprenkelen (“to sprinkle”), German Low German sprenkeln (“to sprinkle; dapple”), German sprenkeln (“to sprinkle”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To cause (a substance) to fall in fine drops (for a liquid substance) or small pieces (for a solid substance).

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Leviticus 14:16:
quote.text: And the priest shall […] sprinkle of the oil with his finger seven times before the Lord.

quote.citation: 1892, Walter Besant, chapter II, in The Ivory Gate […], New York, N.Y.: Harper & Brothers, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: At twilight in the summer […] the mice come out. They […] eat the luncheon crumbs. Mr. Checkly, for instance, always brought his dinner in a paper parcel in his coat-tail pocket, and ate it when so disposed, sprinkling crumbs lavishly […] on the floor.

quote.citation: 1985, Robert Burchfield, The English Language, Oxford: Oxford University Press, page 137:
quote.text: Over the centuries the movement of clans and tribes of people has provided the kind of crop that would emerge if a blind god had sprinkled seeds at random on a field[.]

definitions.definition: (transitive) To cover (an object) by sprinkling a substance on to it.

quote.citation: 2005, Justus Roux, Who's Your Daddy?, page 66:
quote.text: Most of the passengers watched from the enclosed promenade deck, but Sandra found her way to the higher, open promenade where she shivered and watched the city lights fade and the stars sprinkle themselves across a dark blue velvet sky.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To drip in fine drops, sometimes sporadically.
(transitive) To baptize by the application of a few drops, or a small quantity, of water; hence, to cleanse; to purify.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Hebrews 10:22:
quote.text: having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience

definitions.definition: A light covering with a sprinkled substance.

quote.citation: 1979 December 1, Ellen Brook Davis, “David Brill — In Memoriam”, in Gay Community News, volume 7, number 19, page 5:
quote.text: My memory leaves me with a constant and deep burning, my eyes stinging and red from short sprinkles of tears which have been sneaking up on me for days now.

definitions.definition: An aspersorium or utensil for sprinkling.
A small hard piece of sugar and starch, or chocolate, used to decorate cakes etc.
